limitations: Existing reopened-cache byte-for-byte verification was checked against receipt counts and identities; no new cache reread was performed during the active prefix campaign.

Primary 30-pair byte comparisons use exact HTTP bodies, not incomplete per-operation packet attribution. Captured campaign IP totals cover only sender-to-relay leg and include TLS/ACK/retransmissions.
Sender CPU plus receiver-handler CPU is a sum across heterogeneous endpoints; relay/cloudflared and some surrounding origin work are excluded; this is not energy or same-core compute throughput.
Warm operations follow immediately after their seed in the same endpoint process; graph-cache restart/eviction recovery is not this performance result.
Prepared construction belongs to seed; target preparation and terminal cleanup are timed; no successor promotion or multi-update retained-state sequence was measured.
Projected seed amortization assumes the observed marginal cost repeats unchanged; k=1 is the actual observed seed plus one target, while k>1 is not a measured sequence.
Full-copy repeat controls have absent targets; cached repeat benefit is shared by ordinary raw CAS, not unique to DAG or prepared state.
DAG control is current full-fold code; comparisons to historical pre-optimization WAN timings are not contemporaneously paired.
Raw/zstd controls use the same endpoint; zstd uses independent bounded chunks and is not a tuned dictionary/stream compressor or an rsync baseline.

Receiver telemetry starts after HTTP body ingress and request authentication; it includes batch decode, endpoint.handle, hashing/reconstruction, synchronous publication and DAG warming where selected, and reply-frame encoding. It excludes HTTP read/auth parsing, socket writes, relay/cloudflared CPU, and remaining buffer destruction after telemetry is sampled.

Raw/zstd Finish synchronously constructs and attempts to retain an optional DAG; SparseV1 Finish intentionally skips DAG warming. The observed CPU advantage includes that implementation-policy difference and is not an isolated comparison against a minimal raw durable byte sink.

For repeat versus raw_full/zstd_full, candidate seed plus repeat contains two deliveries, whereas the unseeded full-copy control contains one. Their cumulative cost tally is not an equal-work lifecycle head-to-head; seed costs and marginal warm-transfer ratios should be reported separately.

Seed amortization is a mathematical projection of constant per-target cost, not measured repeated state evolution. Prepared successor promotion and its cost are not present in the one-update experiment.
